When I consulted with the dentist, my lower teeth were overlapping, so I decided to get braces. The dentist said it would take at least 3.5 years. I had two teeth extracted before starting braces. During the treatment, the dentist extracted two more teeth. The dentist was very gentle, and everything went smoothly. However, in the third year, the dentist said they forgot to extract one tooth, even though the front teeth were already aligned. This meant they had to pull and move the teeth again. In the fourth year, the dentist said I needed to have my wisdom tooth extracted because it couldn't move any further. If I didn't agree to it, they could only pull it this far – it still wouldn't be perfectly straight, and my teeth would be crooked. I had to agree to have it extracted. It also needed stitches because it was a large, deep-rooted wisdom tooth that had fully erupted and wasn't painful. Imagine how many gaps would be left. At the beginning of 2023, I asked the dentist how many more months it would take, as it seemed like a long time. They said 6 months. Most recently, at the beginning of November, I asked again how much longer, as I'm almost 5 months pregnant. They still said 6 months. (From the beginning to the end of the year, they kept saying 6 months.) The dentist even asked where I lived, and I said Pak Nam, Samut Prakan. They said they also go to Samut Prakan. We declined the offer at Market Village Suvarnabhumi because it wasn't convenient (in my mind, I thought it would be better to stay at the original location, as it's further away). However, the doctor didn't say anything further, nor was there any mention of the branch closing. Then, on November 20th, clinic staff called to inform us that the Seacon Srinakarin branch would be closing and asked us to schedule an appointment to see the doctor at the only branch the doctor had moved to. We could only schedule one appointment. We asked why the branch only informed us now and why the patient had to bear the responsibility for this. How would we travel if it was far away? Also, I'm pregnant and don't have a car; I have to take public transport or a taxi. The staff said they had only just found out as well, some staff members had to find new jobs, and they hadn't followed up at the new branch. We felt this was unacceptable and unacceptable that the company would do this. If the contract with the mall was ending, why wasn't there advance notice? And why wasn't the doctor taking care of patients who were moving branches by allowing them to continue treatment at a branch closer to home? Why wasn't the doctor taking responsibility for continuing treatment for patients who moved branches? In our case, we requested to transfer to the Robinson Samut Prakan branch. When we saw the doctor at Seacon, we paid 500 baht per visit because we were almost finished, but we paid for any equipment malfunctions or other procedures as needed.
It's true that they sent the patient's history to the new branch, but it's up to the doctor whether to accept the case or start over. We feel this is unfair. After all the treatment we've received for so long, we might have to start over and take responsibility again, possibly paying 1000-1500 baht per visit. If it were our case, and we just went to the doctor regularly, missing several months or even a year of orthodontic treatment and having to start over, we could accept that. But the branch is closing, leaving us stranded and having to decide whether to follow up or start over. At least, if the doctor cared for patients who have been with them for a long time, and we're pregnant, could have been kind enough to refer us to a doctor at the branch we're transferring to, and talk to the doctor on our behalf about the situation? We would understand. Today, we saw a new doctor. He examined our teeth for almost 15 minutes, just looking, making us open our mouths, and clench our teeth repeatedly, shaking his head and saying he didn't know what to do or where to start. (We understand that the new doctor's job is difficult when dealing with a case like ours, because the previous doctor had pulled the gaps between our teeth, both upper and lower, so wide that our tongue could stick out.) Finally, the doctor scheduled an appointment with another doctor to see if it was possible. If not, we'll have to discuss a plan to start over. We're wondering how long starting over will take, and we'll be giving birth soon. And now I still have to travel to see the doctor. I thought everything would be finished before the baby is born, but it's dragged on until now. I'm so disappointed to have to go through something like this, especially since I had confidence in this clinic's reputation. At least the clinic should have provided some support.
